classification: source-confirmed stale asynchronous response overwrites current evidence selection; static UI operation proof
title: An evidence inspection response reselects an item the player has left
fact: selectEvidence owns selectedId, active portrait, stage description and conversation. The inspection POST captures the clicked evidence id, but its completion unconditionally calls selectEvidence(updated,button) without checking selectedId or a selection generation. The canonical returned inspection record and current user selection are distinct authorities.
counterexample: Select evidence A, click an A inspection topic to start its POST, select B before that response arrives, then receive valid A response. The completion reselects A, replacing B description and conversation and active portrait despite the latest selection B. All operations are direct existing event handlers; no malformed response, failed request or missing backend gate is needed. No browser/DB execution or actual incident claimed.
limits: Concurrency of multiple A inspections may also permit older data replacement, but record-revision/backend receipt ordering has not been traced and is not accepted here.

Unmount only aborts event listeners and request does not receive that signal; whether detached callbacks affect a later current page is a separate lifecycle question, not asserted by this minimum witness.
Root/global dedup pending; no other-lens coverage or global unique increment claimed.
suggested_connected_remedy: Update the evidence record by stable id independently, then repaint the detail only if the response still belongs to the current selection/generation. Keep latest user selection authoritative and preserve valid historical inspection receipts.
acceptance_contract: A response for an earlier selected evidence item cannot change the user current selection or repaint its stage as another item.
